source_gaps: The Apple Messages page was read in two parts. Its steps came from paraphrase; only the labels Delete and Report Spam, Report Spam, Info and Block Contact are verbatim. The FTC page's first advice is paraphrased, and only the 7726 and ReportFraud sentences are verbatim.

source_refs.title: Report spam and block senders in Messages on iPhone
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; the report can't be made after the message has been replied to; for SMS, MMS, or RCS spam, contact the carrier if the option is not shown
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: 1. Open the Messages app. 2. If the message is not yet opened: swipe left on the message, tap the Delete button, then tap 'Delete and Report Spam.' You can't report a message after you've replied to it. For SMS, MMS, or RCS spam, if you don't see the option, contact your carrier. Reporting doesn't stop the sender, so block them separately if needed.

source_refs.title: Report spam and block senders in Messages on iPhone
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; for an opened message from an unknown sender
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: 1. Open the Messages app. 2. If the message is already opened: look for the 'Report Spam' link at the bottom of the message, tap it, then tap 'Delete and Report Spam.' This link appears for unknown senders. You can't report a message after you've replied to it. Reports for iMessage go to Apple, and the message is permanently deleted from your iPhone.

source_refs.title: Report spam and block senders in Messages on iPhone
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: 1. Open the conversation with that person. 2. Tap their icon at the top. 3. Tap 'Info,' scroll down, then tap 'Block Contact.' Group conversations can't be blocked. You can leave the group or stop its notifications instead. The sender isn't notified that their messages are blocked.

source_refs.title: Report spam in Google Messages
source_refs.applicability: Android phone or tablet using Google Messages
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: 1. On your Android phone or tablet, open Google Messages. 2. Touch and hold the conversation you want to report. 3. Tap 'Block,' then 'Report spam,' then 'OK.' Reporting is optional. You can block a number without reporting it to Google. Reporting sends the spammer's phone number and their last 10 incoming messages to Google.

source_refs.title: Report spam in Google Messages
source_refs.applicability: Android phone or tablet using Google Messages
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: 1. Open the conversation. 2. Tap 'More options,' then 'Details.' 3. Tap 'Block & report spam,' then 'OK.' Reported conversations are moved to the 'Spam & blocked' folder. To undo a spam report, mark the conversation as not spam.

source_refs.title: How to Recognize and Report Spam Text Messages
source_refs.section: What to do with a spam text
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Copy the message and forward it to 7726 (SPAM).
source_refs.model_visible_text: On any phone: Don't tap links in unexpected texts asking for personal or financial information. Contact the company using a phone number or website you know is real. Copy the message and forward it to 7726 (SPAM). Report it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
